title: Raycast 3D set_target_position() fails when code is imported from another scene.
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible on Godot 4.4. Have not checked other versions.
Godot Engine v4.4.stable.official.4c311cbee - https://godotengine.org
Vulkan 1.3.280 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti


### System information

Godot v4.4.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - AMD Ryzen 7 5700 (16 threads)

### Issue description

When raycasting to a target position using set_target_position() different results are achieved depending on whether the set_target_position() section of code is located in the base scene or an imported scene. When the code is in the main_test scene, everything works as I expect. When the code is in an imported scene, the raycast seems to cast to the target position with an offset. 

### Steps to reproduce

Make sure to click Debug -> *Check* Visible Collision Shapes (to see raycasts)

comment one of the following sections of script and uncomment the other to switch between working and non-working code. 

```gdscript
func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	# This is the Raycast code used in the imported scene
	if camera_raycast.is_colliding():
		var target_point = camera_raycast.get_collision_point()
		aiming_raycast.set_target_position(to_local(target_point))
```

This is the Raycast code used in the main_test scene

```gdscript
func _physics_process(_delta):
	if camera_raycast.is_colliding():
		var target_point = camera_raycast.get_collision_point()
		var origin_point = aiming_node.global_position
		aiming_raycast.set_target_position(Vector3(target_point-origin_point))
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[raycast3d issue MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19933320/raycast3d.issue.MRP.zip)
